title: Oregon Gov. Kotek orders halt to data center air, water permitting: ‘It is effectively a temporary moratorium’
key_facts: Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek directed environmental regulators to temporarily stop issuing pollution permits to data centers, which would effectively pause most data center development in Oregon until next summer (July 2027 per OPB's photo caption).

The directive went in a letter to Department of Environmental Quality Director Leah Feldon on Friday (9 Oct 2026); OPB got the exchange from Kotek's office and the nonprofit Oregon Rural Action shared the letter widely.
Kotek also told the agency to stop processing city and county applications to renew or modify wastewater permits to accommodate data centers.
It widens an earlier pause on data center development on state-owned land; without air or water pollution permits most large 'hyperscaler' data centers could not be built on public or private land.

Amazon, which has more than a dozen hyperscale data centers in Morrow and Umatilla Counties, said it was disappointed; an executive said the move could cost Oregon thousands of jobs and billions of dollars in planned investment.
Kotek (Democrat) and her Republican opponent, state Sen. Christine Drazan, both say they favor a moratorium, and data centers are an issue in the governor's race.
Kotek says the pause gives time to weigh recommendations from her Data Center Advisory Committee; lawmakers are expecting many bills when the legislature convenes in January.
quote_evidence: Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek has directed environmental regulators to temporarily stop issuing pollution permits to data centers, which would effectively pause most data center development in Oregon until next summer.
This time limited pause will provide an opportunity for me to evaluate and digest recommendations forthcoming from the Advisory Committee
This directive was issued abruptly, without meaningful stakeholder engagement of the workers, businesses, and municipalities it will affect
why_it_matters_hint: Most large new data centers in Oregon could not get the air and water permits they need until summer 2027.
event_date: Letter sent Fri 9 Oct 2026; made public 13 Oct 2026
